kyle-customer: Hey support — noticed a big discrepancy on our April 7 invoice. Dashboard shows ~120k tokens for the window where our clients were streaming, invoice charges ~1.9M tokens. We usually cancel mid-gen. Any idea what could cause a 15x delta?
sara-support: Sorry about that — can you paste one example request-id and approximate time range? Also did you use the SSE endpoint or the streaming websocket?
kyle-customer: SSE. Example request-id: req_0a9f4e. Window: 2026-04-07T23:10:00Z → 23:45:00Z. Client logs attached (snippet):
```
[SSE] open id=req_0a9f4e
[SSE] recv chunk seq=1 tokens=42
[SSE] client abort (connection close) status=499 at 23:18:12
[SSE] reconnect new_conn id=req_0a9f4e_resume
[SSE] recv chunk seq=2 tokens=310
[SSE] finalizer invoked status=ok tokens_reported=352
```

mike-eng: Thanks, this pattern is familiar. Two things to confirm: 1) whether the client re-used the same conversation/request id on reconnect (looks like it did), and 2) whether the reconnect happened very quickly (<500ms). We have a race in the finalize path where both the old connection close and the resumed connection can trigger final token accounting. When that race succeeds we sometimes count deltas twice and invoice ends up higher than dashboard because dashboard aggregates in a different path.
carmen-sre: Adding details from infra logs for req_0a9f4e (trace id t-7c2):
```
[23:18:12] connection_close handler: generator_id=g-91 finalize_attempt=1 tokens_delta=42
[23:18:12.120] reconnect handler: found stale generator g-91, merge_kvcache, spawn new_connection conn=conn-234
[23:18:12.298] reconnection_finalize path: finalize_attempt=1 tokens_delta=310
[23:18:12.299] billing_emitter: emit_final_count request=req_0a9f4e tokens=352
[23:18:12.300] billing_emitter: emit_final_count request=req_0a9f4e tokens=352  <-- duplicate write (race)
```
This explains the ~2x spike for this request. Over many concurrent reconnects it scales into the millions.
anya-billing: Confirming invoice vs dashboard logic: dashboard shows token totals derived from the streaming aggregation table which collapses by generator_id and uses the last-seen finalizer. The invoice pipeline, however, consumes "finalize" events from the emitter topic; duplicates there will be additive unless the emitter deduplicates on (org, generator_id, finalize_id). We currently had a gap where finalize_id was sometimes empty for quick reconnects.
sara-support: For the customer -> immediate next steps: 1) we're opening an internal incident to track this, 2) we will run a targeted reconciliation for your org to remove duplicate finalize events for that date range, 3) we will provide timeline and a credit if the reconciliation shows duplicate charges. @anya-billing can you run the ad-hoc script?
anya-billing: On it. Running dry-run now against req prefix req_0a9f4e.* — I see ~1,342 duplicate finalize events across that org for the window. I will prepare a remediation plan. We will not invoice duplicates; ops will create the adjustment.
mike-eng: Longer term fix: adding idempotency token to finalize events and ensure billing_emitter writes with if-not-exists semantics. I opened PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/487 (branch fix/sse-finalize-idempotency). Patch summary: track finalize_id per generator, ignore duplicate finalize attempts, and add 200ms coalescing window on reconnect to prevent the close+reconnect race.
carmen-sre: Also adding a temporary metric and alert: metric streaming.finalize_duplicates by org. Deployed to staging; will roll to prod after quick smoke.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-452 — "SSE finalize race causing duplicate billing emits" https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-452
kyle-customer: Thanks — appreciate the quick response. Can you confirm ETA for reconciliation/credit? Our finance team needs a number for accruals.
anya-billing: ETA: dry-run complete, reconciliation script ready, planning to run for affected orgs tonight (2026-04-08 02:00 UTC). If results match dry-run we'll apply credit within 48 hours and follow up with an itemized statement.
mike-eng: For reproducibility (internal): quick curl flow to repro locally — run these in separate terminals to simulate the race: 
```
# open stream
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.dev/v1/streams?req_id=req_test \
  -d '{"prompt":"...","stream":true}'
# immediately kill (ctrl-c) then reopen using same req_id
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.dev/v1/streams?req_id=req_test \
  -d '{"prompt":"...","stream":true}'
```
That will produce duplicate finalize events in the pre-patch runtime.
anya-billing: After reconciliation runs I'll DM you the statement and cc support.
kyle-customer: Great — please keep me posted in this thread. We'll pause streaming rollouts until you confirm the fix. Thanks. :pray:
